findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, so it receives a public IP and can be reached from the internet. Combined with the MySQL listener on 3306 this exposes the database service directly to external attackers.
storage_encrypted = false leaves the MySQL data files, automated backups, and snapshots unencrypted, so anyone gaining access to the underlying storage can read the catalog data.

The master password is supplied as a plaintext variable (var.password) and referenced directly in the resource and in the EC2 user_data PHP file, so the database credential is stored in Terraform state and in cleartext on the instance filesystem.
The master username is the fixed, guessable value "admin", which removes a layer of protection against credential-stuffing and brute-force attempts against the publicly reachable database.

The inbound rule permits MySQL (3306/tcp) from the entire VPC CIDR block rather than from the application instance or a dedicated application security group, so any workload in the VPC can reach the database.
The database security group allows all outbound traffic (protocol -1, 0.0.0.0/0), which permits data exfiltration or lateral movement from a compromised database.

The attached policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", giving the EC2 instance full administrative control of storage, compute, and database services in the account if the role is ever assumed.
The EC2 user_data embeds the database password, username, and endpoint in a PHP include file written to the instance, exposing credentials to anyone with instance metadata or filesystem access.
The AMI lookup filters on a suspicious name pattern (amzn2-ami-hvm-*-x86_64-portal-disk) rather than a trusted Amazon image, so it may resolve to an unintended or attacker-supplied image.

The output exposes the database endpoint, and output.catalog_app_public_dns exposes the instance's public DNS name, both of which aid reconnaissance against the publicly reachable database and application.
